newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar slackens vs yen in Tokyo before trade data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar slackens vs yen in Tokyo before trade data.

text.p: 0616 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar edged lower versus the yen by late Tokyo trade on Tuesday as concern over Japan's burgeoning trade surplus grew ahead of the release of the country's May trade data early on Wednesday, dealers said.
Traders said that the dollar could be fragile in the near term but they were mixed about whether a sharp increase in Japan's surplus would invite a fresh wave of dollar sales.

"The European issue has settled down for the moment and the market is now focusing on (U.S.-Japan) trade issues," a dealer at a trust bank said. On Monday, EU finance ministers reached a compromise on a stability pact at the EU summit in Amsterdam.

Economists polled by Reuters forecast on average that Japan's trade surplus, due at 8.50 a.m., would rise to 548.5 billion yen, from a surplus of 229 billion yen a year earlier. Their forecasts ranged from 400 billion to 760 billion yen.
After trimming earlier gains due to sales by exporters and overseas funds, the dollar was supported by talk of bids from Japanese life insurers at 112.80-113.00 yen.

Traders were also wary of selling dollars aggressively due to the bitter memory of getting stung last week after their short-positions were quickly squeezed following the talk-up of the dollar by a Japanese finance ministry official.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday that the ministry would deal appropriately with an excessive rise or fall in the yen.
He also said it was unlikely there would be heated discussions over Japan's surplus at the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations' summit meeting in Denver from June 20 to 22.
"I am expecting the traditional pattern of sell-on-rumour and buy-on-fact to take place after the trade data," said a bank dealer.

But a dealer at a Japanese bank said the dollar is likely to test the downside, with stop-loss dollar sales seen below 112.70 yen. "The total volume of insurers' buying is estimated at around $300 million, with selling interest above 113.30 yen to be much larger," he added.
"Participants here might have already factored in a rise in the trade surplus, but overseas operators may not have fully priced it in yet," he added.
The bank dealer said verbal intervention by the Japanese authorities may be less effective than the previous time since there has not been a large accumulation of speculative short positions.
"The market isn't really short so they're a bit nervous about it coming down," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
He said the dollar/mark looked well-bid at around 1.7270 marks, while the mark/yen's topside was heavy.
"A lot of people missed the move up in mark/yen at the end of last week and early this week so there's healthy interest in selling marks on any rally," he said.
The mark was standing at 65.40 yen at 0644 GMT against 65.51 yen in early trade.
The dollar closed at 113.24/27 yen and 1.7305/15 marks in New York on Monday.
